answers.question: what-to-bring
answers.title_en: Wedding — Guest — What to bring
answers.title_sm: Faʻaipoipoga — Mālō — Mea e aumai
guidance_en: A cash gift in an envelope marked clearly with your name. Even a modest amount is welcome — what matters is that you are present and contributing.
If you are close to either family, ask if they are collecting ʻie tōga; if so, you may add one.
Do not bring elaborate wrapped gifts (toasters, blenders). Cash and ʻie tōga are the cultural norm.
guidance_sm: O se meaalofa tupe i totonu o se teutusi ma lou igoa. E lava lava se aofaʻi itiiti — o le mea tāua o lou auai ma le fesoasoani.
Pe afai e te vavalalata ma se tasi o aiga, fesili pe o loʻo aoaoina ʻie tōga; pe afai e ioe, e mafai ona e faʻaopoopo se tasi.
Aua ni meaalofa tetele ua afifia (toaster, blender). O le tupe ma le ʻie tōga le mea masani o le aganuʻu.

answers.question: what-to-wear
answers.title_en: Wedding — Guest — What to wear
answers.title_sm: Faʻaipoipoga — Mālō — Lāʻei
guidance_en: Women: puletasi or formal dress. Shoulders covered. Modest length. Head covered for the church service.
Men: ie faitaga and white shirt with tie, or full suit.
Avoid bright tourist prints, very short hems, or anything beachy.
guidance_sm: Tamāʻitaʻi: puletasi po o se ofu aloaʻia. Pulou tauʻau. Ofu e talafeagai. Pulou le ulu mo le lotu.
Aliʻi: ie faitaga ma se ofu paʻepaʻe ma le fusi ua, po o se suti atoatoa.
Aua le ofuina o mea faʻaturisi, ofu pupuʻu, po o mea o le matafaga.

answers.question: when-to-arrive
answers.title_en: Wedding — Guest — When to arrive
answers.title_sm: Faʻaipoipoga — Mālō — Taimi e taunuʻu ai
guidance_en: Arrive 30 minutes before the stated church start time. Samoan services start on time; the reception rarely does.
For the reception, arrive at the stated time — you may wait, but do not walk in after the matai have been seated.
If you must arrive late, wait at the entrance for a break in the lāuga before finding a seat.
guidance_sm: Taunuʻu i le 30 minute aʻo leʻi amata le lotu. E amata i lona taimi le sauniga; ae le masani ai le faleoʻo.
Mo le faleoʻo, taunuʻu i le taimi ua taʻua — e mafai ona faʻatali, ae aua le ulufale pe a uma ona nonofo matai.
Pe afai e te tuai, faʻatali i le faitotoʻa seʻia oʻo i se malaga i le lāuga.

answers.question: what-to-bring
answers.title_en: Wedding — Hosting family — What to prepare
answers.title_sm: Faʻaipoipoga — Aiga talimālō — Mea e saunia
guidance_en: Confer with your matai/saʻo on the aigaʼs collective contribution.
ʻIe tōga: many — for presentation to the other family and for distribution to attending matai.
Substantial food: umu, additional cooked dishes, drinks.
Cash for sua, taupou ula gifts, and the wider exchange.
Take an inventory beforehand — quantity will be noted.
guidance_sm: Fesili i lou matai/saʻo e uiga i le fesoasoani a le aiga atoa.
ʻIe tōga: e tele — mo le isi aiga ma mo matai uma o le aoao.
Meaʻai e tele: umu, meaʻai faʻaopoopo, mea inu.
Tupe mo le sua, ula a le taupou, ma le tuʻufaʻatasiga atoa.
Fai se lisi aʻo leʻi oʻo le aso — e faʻamauina.

answers.question: what-to-bring
answers.title_en: Wedding — Matai — What to prepare
answers.title_sm: Faʻaipoipoga — Matai — Sauniuniga
guidance_en: Confer with your saʻo and the aiga potopoto before deciding your personal contribution.
You will be called in the ʻava; be present in the matai line and respond to your suafa.
Named ʻie tōga carry more weight than count alone — bring what represents your standing.
Prepare a short lāuga in case you are asked to speak on behalf of the aiga.
guidance_sm: Fesili i lou saʻo ma le aiga potopoto aʻo leʻi filifili lau fesoasoani.
O le a taʻua oe i le ʻava; nofo i le laina o matai, ma tali i lou suafa.
E sili atu le tāua o ʻie tōga ua i ai igoa, nai lo le aofaʻi. Aumai le mea e fetaui ma lou tulaga.
Sauni se lāuga puʻupuʻu, atonu e fesili atu oe e tautala mo le aiga.

answers.question: what-to-bring
answers.title_en: Funeral — Visiting family — What to bring
answers.title_sm: Maliu — Aiga asiasi — Mea e aumai
guidance_en: Confer with your matai before going. The aigaʼs contribution will usually be coordinated together.
ʻIe tōga: the heaviest contribution. The number is decided by your matai.
Cash in named envelopes per branch of the aiga.
Food contribution if requested by the bereaved aiga.
Plan to stay for the lāuga, the meal, and the burial — not just one of these.
guidance_sm: Fesili i lou matai aʻo leʻi alu. E masani lava ona soalaupule fesoasoani a le aiga atoa.
ʻIe tōga: o le fesoasoani sili ona mamafa. E filifili e lou matai le aofaʻi.
Tupe i teutusi ua i ai igoa o lala taʻitasi o le aiga.
Meaʻai pe afai ua manaʻomia e le aiga ua tigāina.
Fuafua e te nofo mo le lāuga, le taumafataga, ma le falelauasiga — ae le na o le tasi.

answers.question: what-to-bring
answers.title_en: Funeral — Guest — What to bring
answers.title_sm: Maliu — Mālō — Mea e aumai
guidance_en: A cash contribution in a named envelope. This is the minimum — every visitor is expected to contribute.
If you are close to the family, ask if you should bring ʻie tōga or food. Do not assume — ask.
Black or very dark clothing. No exceptions.
guidance_sm: Se fesoasoani tupe i se teutusi ma lou igoa. O le mea sili ona pito i lalo — e faʻamoemoeina mālō uma e fesoasoani.
Pe afai e te vavalalata ma le aiga, fesili pe e aumai ʻie tōga po o meaʻai. Aua neʻi manatu naʻo oe — fesili.
Lāʻei uliuli pe pogisa lava. E leai se tuusaunoaga.

answers.question: how-to-greet
answers.title_en: Funeral — Greeting the bereaved
answers.title_sm: Maliu — Faʻafeiloaʻi le aiga ua tigāina
guidance_en: Approach softly. A handshake or quiet embrace is appropriate. Lower your voice.
Use mālō le onosaʻi (well borne) or alofa atu (love to you).
Do not ask how the deceased died. Do not stay too long in the line if many are waiting.
guidance_sm: Faʻalatalata ma le filemū. E talafeagai se lulu lima po o se fusi puʻupuʻu. Tautala lemū.
Faʻaaogā mālō le onosaʻi po o alofa atu.
Aua e te fesili pe na maliu faʻapefea. Aua le tu umi i le laina pe afai e tele e faʻatali.

answers.question: what-to-bring
answers.title_en: Funeral — Bereaved aiga — What to prepare
answers.title_sm: Maliu — Aiga tigāina — Mea e saunia
guidance_en: Notify the extended aiga, church, and matai of the village early — through the failauga.
Prepare space to receive visiting aiga over multiple days, and to record contributions.
Umu and food for many. Every visitor eats.
Designate a tulāfale to receive lāuga and call out contributions publicly.
Prepare the fanua (family plot) for burial ahead of time.
guidance_sm: Faʻasilasila i le aiga potopoto, le lotu, ma matai o le nuʻu — e ala i le failauga.
Sauni le nofoaga e talia ai aiga asiasi i aso e tele, ma faʻamauina fesoasoani.
Umu ma meaʻai mo tagata e toʻatele. E ʻai mālō uma.
Tofia se tulāfale e talia lāuga, ma taʻua aloaʻia fesoasoani.
Sauni le fanua o le aiga mo le falelauasiga.

answers.question: how-to-give
answers.title_en: Funeral — Matai — Delivering the aigaʼs contribution
answers.title_sm: Maliu — Matai — Tuʻuina atu o le fesoasoani
guidance_en: Lead the aigaʼs procession to the gate. Do not enter until welcomed by the host tulāfale.
Your tulāfale delivers the lāuga first: God, the deceased, the aiga, then the gift.
Present ʻie tōga first, then cash envelopes named aloud, then food.
Wait for the host acknowledgement before sitting.
guidance_sm: Taʻimua i le savavaliga o le aiga i le faitotoʻa. Aua le ulufale seʻia faʻafeiloaʻia e le tulāfale o le aiga.
E muamua lāuga a lau tulāfale: le Atua, le ua maliu, le aiga, ona sosoʻo ai lea ma le meaalofa.
Faʻaali muamua ʻie tōga, ona sosoʻo ai lea ma teutusi tupe ua taʻua aloaʻia, ona sosoʻo ai ma meaʻai.
Faʻatali le faʻafetai a le aiga aʻo leʻi nofo.

answers.question: what-to-bring
answers.title_en: Faʻalavelave — Guest — What to bring
answers.title_sm: Faʻalavelave — Mālō — Mea e aumai
guidance_en: A cash contribution is the baseline for any faʻalavelave you are invited to. Name your envelope.
For a heavy faʻalavelave (funeral, saofaʻi, church dedication), ask your matai whether ʻie tōga are also expected of you.
For a lighter one (birthday, graduation), cash and presence are usually enough.
guidance_sm: O se fesoasoani tupe le mea muamua i soʻo se faʻalavelave e valaʻau atu ai oe. Tusi lou igoa i le teutusi.
Mo se faʻalavelave mamafa (maliu, saofaʻi, faʻapaʻiaga falesā), fesili i lou matai pe e faʻamoemoe atu oe e aumai ʻie tōga.
Mo se faʻalavelave māmā (aso fanau, faʻauʻuga), e lava le tupe ma lou auai.

answers.question: how-to-give
answers.title_en: Faʻalavelave — Visiting aiga — How to give
answers.title_sm: Faʻalavelave — Aiga asiasi — Tuʻuina atu
guidance_en: Move as one aiga. Do not deliver contributions individually — the collective act is the honour.
Your tulāfale offers a lāuga on arrival. Only after the host receives may the gifts be laid out.
ʻIe tōga first, cash second (each envelope named), food third.
Wait for the host tulāfaleʼs acknowledgement of each item before proceeding.
guidance_sm: Alu faʻatasi le aiga. Aua le tuʻuina atu fesoasoani taʻitasi — o le gaoioiga faʻatasi o le faʻaaloalo.
E ofo mai e lau tulāfale se lāuga i le taunuʻuga. Pe a maeʻa ona talia e le aiga, ona faʻaali ai lea o meaalofa.
ʻIe tōga muamua, tupe lua (taʻua taʻitasi teutusi), meaʻai tolu.
Faʻatali le faʻafetai a le tulāfale o le aiga i mea taʻitasi, aʻo leʻi faʻaauau.

answers.question: how-to-give
answers.title_en: Faʻalavelave — Hosting aiga — How to receive
answers.title_sm: Faʻalavelave — Aiga talimālō — Talia o fesoasoani
guidance_en: Designate a tulāfale to call each contribution aloud as it lands — name of giver, aiga, item.
Keep a written or mental register. The names read out today are the obligations owed tomorrow.
Every contribution deserves acknowledgement in the moment. Silence read as disrespect.
The saʻo speaks at the close: thanks to God, thanks to each contributing aiga by name.
guidance_sm: Tofia se tulāfale e taʻu aloaʻia le fesoasoani a ō mai — igoa o le tagata, le aiga, ma le meaalofa.
Faʻamau i pepa pe i le manatu. O igoa ua taʻua i le aso nei, o tiute ia o taeao.
E tatau ona faʻafetai i fesoasoani taʻitasi i le taimi. O le filemū e faʻamatalaina ai le lē faʻaaloalo.
E tautala le saʻo i le faʻaiʻuga: faʻafetai i le Atua, faʻafetai i aiga taʻitasi ua fesoasoani, i o latou igoa.

answers.question: how-to-greet
answers.title_en: ʻAva — Guest — How to behave in the ceremony
answers.title_sm: ʻAva — Mālō — Amio i le sauniga
guidance_en: Sit cross-legged, quiet, legs never pointed at the tanoa or the matai.
Do not talk during the mixing or distribution. Silence is the mark of the sauniga.
If a cup is offered to you (rare as a guest), receive with both hands, pour a small libation to the ground, drink in one, return the cup.
Never step over the fau, the tanoa, or in front of a seated matai.
guidance_sm: Nofo faʻavaevae, filemū, aua neʻi faʻasaga vae i le tanoa po o matai.
Aua le tautala aʻo palu ma tufa le ʻava. O le filemū o le faʻailoga o le sauniga.
Pe afai e ofoina atu se ipu ia te oe (e seāseā mo se mālō), talia i lima e lua, sasaa se vaega itiiti i le eleʻele, inu i le tasi, toe tuʻu atu le ipu.
Aua le sopoia le fau, le tanoa, po o matai o loʻo nonofo.

answers.question: how-to-greet
answers.title_en: ʻAva — Matai — Receiving your cup
answers.title_sm: ʻAva — Matai — Talia lou ipu
guidance_en: When the tulāfale calls your suafa, respond quietly to acknowledge.
Receive the cup with both hands. Pour the taumafa (libation) onto the ground or into a shell before drinking.
Drink in a single motion. Return the cup with both hands.
Do not begin any lāuga or discussion until every cup in the order has been served.
guidance_sm: Pe a taʻua e le tulāfale lou suafa, tali atu ma le filemū.
Talia le ipu i lima e lua. Sasaa le taumafa i le eleʻele po o se ipu niu aʻo leʻi inu.
Inu i le tasi sapasapaiga. Toe tuʻu atu le ipu i lima e lua.
Aua le amata soʻo se lāuga po o se talanoaga, seʻia maeʻa le tufa o ipu uma.

answers.question: how-to-give
answers.title_en: ʻAva — Tulāfale — Calling the cups
answers.title_sm: ʻAva — Tulāfale — Taʻuina o ipu
guidance_en: Confirm the rank order of aliʻi and tulāfale present before the mixing begins.
Call the first cup for the most senior aliʻi, naming their suafa in full.
Continue in strict order: aliʻi (by rank), tulāfale (by rank), then any visitors and lower-rank matai.
Never skip or reverse the order — the order is the ceremony.
guidance_sm: Faʻamaonia le faʻasologa o le mamalu o aliʻi ma tulāfale, aʻo leʻi amata le palu.
Taʻu le ipu muamua mo le aliʻi silisili, ma faʻaigoa lona suafa atoa.
Faʻaauau i le faʻasologa: aliʻi (i lona faʻasologa), tulāfale (i lona faʻasologa), ona sosoʻo ai lea ma mālō ma isi matai.
Aua neʻi soona faʻasese le faʻasologa — o le faʻasologa lava lea o le sauniga.

answers.question: what-to-bring
answers.title_en: ʻAva — Host aiga — What to prepare
answers.title_sm: ʻAva — Aiga talimālō — Sauniuniga
guidance_en: ʻAva root (aʻa), well dried.
The tanoa (carved bowl), the fau (strainer of hibiscus bast), and enough ipu (cups) for every matai present.
A skilled taupou or taufa to mix.
Cleared, quiet space; no phones, no children running through.
guidance_sm: Aʻa o le ʻava, ua mago lelei.
O le tanoa, le fau, ma ipu e lava mo matai uma.
Se taupou po o se taufa ua tomai i le palu.
Nofoaga ua faʻamamā, filemū; leai ni telefoni, ni tamaiti tamomoʻe.

answers.question: what-to-bring
answers.title_en: Saofaʻi — Bestowing aiga — What to prepare
answers.title_sm: Saofaʻi — Aiga tuʻuina — Sauniuniga
guidance_en: ʻIe tōga in significant number — this is a major faʻalavelave.
Cash for the village fono (consult your saʻo on the amount).
ʻAva root.
Pigs, taro, and an umu sufficient to feed the village fono.
Formal lāʻei for the candidate and all aiga members at the saofaʻi.
guidance_sm: ʻIe tōga e tele — o se faʻalavelave mamafa.
Tupe mo le fono a le nuʻu (fesili i lou saʻo mo le aofaʻi).
Aʻa o le ʻava.
Puaʻa, talo, ma se umu ua lava e fafaga ai le fono a le nuʻu.
Lāʻei aloaʻia mo le sui ma le aiga atoa i le saofaʻi.

answers.question: how-to-greet
answers.title_en: Saofaʻi — New matai — First words
answers.title_sm: Saofaʻi — Matai fou — Uluaʻi upu
guidance_en: When your new suafa is called for your first ʻava cup, respond quietly — this is your acceptance.
Speak last in the lāuga. Speak briefly. Thank God, the fono of the nuʻu, and the aiga.
Do not celebrate. The saofaʻi is not a promotion — it is a burden acknowledged.
From this day, you answer to the aiga, the nuʻu, and the lotu. Say so plainly.
guidance_sm: Pe a taʻua lou suafa fou mo lau uluaʻi ipu ʻava, tali ma le filemū — o lou talia lea o le suafa.
Tautala mulimuli i lāuga. Tautala puʻupuʻu. Faʻafetai i le Atua, i le fono a le nuʻu, ma le aiga.
Aua le faʻafiafia. E le o se siitaga le saofaʻi — o se avega ua talia.
Talu mai lenei aso, e te tali atu i le aiga, i le nuʻu, ma le lotu. Taʻu manino atu.

answers.question: what-to-wear
answers.title_en: Saofaʻi — Guest — What to wear
answers.title_sm: Saofaʻi — Mālō — Lāʻei
guidance_en: Formal. Do not dress down for a saofaʻi — it is one of the heaviest cultural moments an aiga will host.
Women: puletasi, modest, shoulders covered.
Men: ie faitaga and white shirt with tie, or a dark suit.
No prints, no beachwear, no sandals.
guidance_sm: Aloaʻia. Aua le māmā le lāʻei mo le saofaʻi — o se tasi o taimi sili ona mamafa i le aganuʻu.
Tamāʻitaʻi: puletasi, faʻaaloalo, pulou tauʻau.
Aliʻi: ie faitaga ma se ofu paʻepaʻe ma le fusi ua, po o se suti pogisa.
Aua ni mea faʻaturisi, ni mea o le matafaga, ni sevae māmā.

answers.question: what-to-bring
answers.title_en: Saofaʻi — Visiting aiga — What to bring
answers.title_sm: Saofaʻi — Aiga asiasi — Mea e aumai
guidance_en: ʻIe tōga in respectful number — reflecting your aigaʼs relationship to the bestowing aiga.
Cash in named envelopes.
Formal lāʻei.
Time — a saofaʻi runs long. Do not plan a departure before the closing lāuga.
guidance_sm: ʻIe tōga faʻaaloalo — e faʻatatau i le faiā o lou aiga i le aiga tuʻuina.
Tupe i teutusi ua taʻua igoa.
Lāʻei aloaʻia.
Taimi — e umi le saofaʻi. Aua neʻi fuafua e alu ese aʻo leʻi maeʻa le lāuga faʻaiʻuga.

answers.question: what-to-bring
answers.title_en: White Sunday — What to prepare
answers.title_sm: Lotu a Tamaiti — Mea e saunia
guidance_en: White lāʻei for every child of the aiga.
A memorised verse or song per child — even the youngest.
A larger-than-usual Sunday lunch. The children are served first.
No gifts to adults — this day belongs to the children.
guidance_sm: Lāʻei paʻepaʻe mo tamaiti uma o le aiga.
Se tauloto po o se pese ua sauni — e oʻo lava i e laiti.
Se toʻonaʻi e tele atu nai lo le masani. E muaʻi tausi tamaiti.
Aua ni meaalofa i tagata matutua — o le aso e mo tamaiti.

answers.question: cant-contribute
answers.title_en: I cannot contribute the full amount
answers.title_sm: E lē mafai ona ou faʻataunuʻu atoatoa
guidance_en: Communicate as early as possible. Speak to your matai, your saʻo, or — if you are external — directly to the host aigaʼs tulāfale.
Use the word faʻatoesega (apology). State plainly: 'O loʻu faʻatoesega' — this is my apology.
Send what you can with respect. A small contribution well-named and accompanied by an explanation is honoured.
Do not send nothing without word. Silence is the failure; partial contribution with communication is not.
guidance_sm: Talanoa vave. Fesili i lou matai, lou saʻo, po o — pe afai e te i fafo — faʻasaʻo atu i le tulāfale o le aiga e talimalo.
Faʻaaogā le upu faʻatoesega. Taʻu manino atu: ʻO loʻu faʻatoesega.ʻ
Tuʻuina atu le mea e mafai ma le faʻaaloalo. O se fesoasoani itiiti ma le igoa ma le faʻamatalaga e faʻaaloalogia.
Aua le auina atu se mea aunoa ma le tala. O le filemū — o le sese; o le fesoasoani itiiti ma le talanoaga — e lē sese.

answers.question: where-to-sit
answers.title_en: Where do I sit as a guest?
answers.title_sm: O fea e nofo ai se mālō?
guidance_en: Not in the matai row — that is the front. Behind the matai of your aiga, or in the guest seating indicated by the host tulāfale.
Wait to be shown; do not pick a seat alone.
If sitting on the floor in a fale samoa, keep legs crossed or tucked under — never pointed at the matai.
guidance_sm: Aua i le laina o matai — o luma lena. I tua o matai o lou aiga, po o le nofoaga o mālō ua faʻasino e le tulāfale.
Faʻatali seʻi faʻasino atu; aua naʻo oe e faʻaiʻu.
Pe afai o le a nofo i lalo i se fale samoa, faʻatautau vae i lalo — aua neʻi faʻasaga vae i matai.
